## Which file do I need?

Cognitive Terrain runs in your web browser. Nothing to install.

| You want to… | Download |
|---|---|
| Play straight away on any computer | **cognitive-terrain-0.18.html**, then double-click it to open in your browser |
| Read the rules | **Cognitive-Terrain-Field-Manual-0.18.pdf** |
| A one-sheet summary to print, two-sided | **Cognitive-Terrain-Player-Aid-0.18.pdf** |
| Run it for a group, build campaigns, see why it works | **Cognitive-Terrain-Practitioners-Manual-0.18.pdf** |
| Hear each week read aloud (optional) | the **Immersive Briefings** voice pack, on its own release: **voice-emma-1** |

Two-player games work as long as both players use version 0.18.

## What's new

- **Browser only.** Cognitive Terrain is supported in the browser for now:
  play it online from the playtest page, or download the HTML file and open
  it. There are no installers for this version; the manuals say so.
- **A new layout of the mind on every map.** The five areas no longer sit in
  the same place every game. Trust is always at the middle; Decide is a lobe
  somewhere on the rim; and Act, Notice and Interpret follow it around the
  ring, so the loop always runs in order (Notice → Interpret → Decide → Act →
  back to Notice) and each area borders the next one in the loop.
  - Every map has the same area sizes: Notice 6 nodes, Interpret 6, Decide 8,
    Act 6, Trust 4. Before, they ranged from 2 to 11 depending on the map.
  - Entry points sit at the outer edge of their area (Social Media on the side
    of Trust that faces Act); Top Leadership sits deep inside Decide.
  - Balance checked over 200 computer-vs-computer games per campaign: Blue's
    win rate across all campaigns, early wins, and how fast an idle Blue falls
    are close to 0.17.4's (Blue wins 50% of games against 48%; 30% end early
    against 27%). Some campaigns moved: The Lake Referendum (39% → 60% Blue
    wins) and The Valmora Vote (50% → 58%) got easier for Blue; Collision at
    Varrin Reef (39% → 33%) and Winter Grid (59% → 50%) got harder.
    Veteran is about as hard as before.
- **Decision-loop overlay that matches the map.** The outlines of Notice,
  Interpret, Decide, Act and Trust are worked out from each map's own nodes, so
  every node sits inside its own area and no other, and the outlines move with
  the map. Before, the rounded outlines could leave a node outside its area or
  inside a neighbour's (Social Media, a Trust node, could look as if it were in
  Act).
- **Stacked effects.** When a node has more than one effect, the Watch Team
  and Prebunk tags stack instead of printing over each other, and the node's
  label lists each status on its own line. Names on the map keep clear of
  them.
- **A shorter, steadier tutorial.** Eleven short steps, one idea each,
  updated for this build: the areas that move from map to map, entry points,
  the new move preview, the spread grade, the score, defences and the
  calendar. Card, area and entry-point names come from the game, so they match
  the map and the PLAIN / MILITARY words.
  - The tutorial panel stays docked in one corner above the timeline. It only
    switches sides when it would cover what the step points at.
  - Steps never move on by themselves. A task ticks when it is done and stays
    ticked; BACK, NEXT and the step dots go to any step, including ones you
    clicked past. ✕ CLOSE ends it; Settings ⚙ › TUTORIAL reopens it.
- **Immersive Briefings never start by themselves.** The broadcast in the
  week in review now waits for **▶ LISTEN**; before, it started reading as soon
  as the week in review opened and could carry on into your next turn. Once
  you start it, it still plays on after you continue, with an ON AIR tab to
  stop it.
- The manuals' pictures are retaken on the new maps; their worked examples are
  unchanged. The Field Manual explains the new map layout (2.3) and that
  Immersive Briefings wait for LISTEN (15.3).
- No rule changes, but maps are laid out differently, so **two-player codes
  work only between 0.18 builds**.
